source.description: One reviewed six-panel graphite-and-colored-pencil contact sheet cropped into five cumulative process frames and one finished master.
source.notes: Keep one unbranded vintage sewing machine in a stable three-quarter side view with one arched body, one right handwheel, one top spool, a visible thread path, needle and presser foot, fabric under the foot, a wooden base, restrained ornament, and one broken shadow. No lettering, logo, scissors, buttons, or extra notions.

process_strategy: Reserve the machine body, wheel, spool, thread route, needle, presser foot, fabric, wooden base, ornament, and shadow in pale construction before darkening the silhouette; clarify the mechanical overlaps before hatching and color; limit the final panel to stronger keeper lines, existing values, and restrained surface cleanup.

final_elements.name: arched cast-iron body needle column wooden platform and side thickness
final_elements.description: One stable vintage machine silhouette with a high arched arm, vertical needle column, visible side thickness, and a shallow rectangular wooden platform.

final_elements.name: one handwheel one spool thread path needle presser foot and fabric
final_elements.description: One large right-side handwheel, one small spool on the top pin, one continuous thread route, one needle and presser foot, and one folded fabric rectangle passing under the foot.

final_elements.name: engraved panel graphite hatching and broken cast shadow
final_elements.description: A simple wordless ornamental side panel, short curved graphite hatches on the metal, wood-grain marks on the base, fabric strokes, and one broken tabletop shadow.

final_elements.name: charcoal burgundy brass blue and warm-wood pencil tint
final_elements.description: Restrained charcoal and burgundy metal, tiny brass hardware accents, muted blue fabric, and warm-brown wood applied over visible graphite and paper highlights.

rejection_checks: Keep one sewing machine, one three-quarter side view, one crop, and one scale in all six panels.
The arched body, handwheel, spool, thread route, needle, presser foot, fabric, platform, ornament, and shadow must stay in the same positions after they appear.
Reserve the wheel and fabric overlaps before darkening the body and platform; do not erase keeper lines to fake the assembly.
Do not add lettering, a logo, a second spool, scissors, buttons, loose notions, a table scene, border, or decorative frame.
The final panel may not introduce a new mechanism, ornament, fold, shadow shape, or color area.
The finish must look like tactile graphite and colored pencil on paper, not a rasterized vector, polished product illustration, or glossy AI rendering.
